pages.text: On Saturday morning, Dufie took her little brother Kpakpo into the yard. “Look!” said Kpakpo. “Something dark is following us!” Dufie laughed. “That is our shadow.”
sentences: On Saturday morning, Dufie took her little brother Kpakpo into the yard.
“Look!” said Kpakpo.
“Something dark is following us!” Dufie laughed.
“That is our shadow.”
pages.alt: In warm morning sunlight, Dufie and little Kpakpo stand in their sandy compound yard pointing happily at two long dark shadows stretching beside them.

pages.text: Dufie held up her hand in the sunlight. A dark shape appeared on the ground. “A shadow is made when something blocks the light,” she said. “The light cannot go through my hand.” She was careful never to look straight at the sun.
sentences: Dufie held up her hand in the sunlight.
A dark shape appeared on the ground.
“A shadow is made when something blocks the light,” she said.
“The light cannot go through my hand.” She was careful never to look straight at the sun.
pages.alt: Dufie holds one open hand up in the morning sun, casting a crisp hand-shaped shadow onto the warm earth while Kpakpo crouches to look.

pages.text: Dufie put a stone, a green leaf, and a clear plastic cup on the ground. The stone made a dark shadow. The leaf made a lighter shadow. The clear cup made almost no shadow, because the light passed right through it.
sentences: Dufie put a stone, a green leaf, and a clear plastic cup on the ground.
The stone made a dark shadow.
The leaf made a lighter shadow.
The clear cup made almost no shadow, because the light passed right through it.
pages.alt: Close view on sunlit ground showing a grey stone casting a dark shadow, a green leaf casting a soft translucent shadow, and a clear cup letting light pass through.

pages.text: They checked their shadows in the morning, at noon, and in the afternoon. In the morning, their shadows were long. At noon, when the sun was high overhead, their shadows were very short. In the afternoon, they grew long again.
sentences: They checked their shadows in the morning, at noon, and in the afternoon.
In the morning, their shadows were long.
At noon, when the sun was high overhead, their shadows were very short.
In the afternoon, they grew long again.
pages.alt: Bright midday scene in the sunny yard where Dufie and Kpakpo look down in wonder at their tiny, short noon shadows right beneath their sandals.

pages.text: At night, Kpakpo could not find his shadow. “It has gone!” he cried. Dufie shone a hand torch toward his arm, and a shadow appeared on the wall. “Here it is,” she said. “A shadow needs light. Without light, there is no shadow.”
sentences: At night, Kpakpo could not find his shadow.
“It has gone!” he cried.
Dufie shone a hand torch toward his arm, and a shadow appeared on the wall.
“Here it is,” she said.
“A shadow needs light.
Without light, there is no shadow.”
pages.alt: Inside a cosy dim room at night, Dufie shines a bright hand torch onto Kpakpo’s raised arm, casting a clear arm shadow onto the plain wall.

pages.text: Dufie summed up what they had learned: a shadow is made when light is blocked, shadows are long in the morning and afternoon and short at noon, and every shadow needs light. Kpakpo clapped his hands. “Now we can teach Mama!”
sentences: Dufie summed up what they had learned: a shadow is made when light is blocked, shadows are long in the morning and afternoon and short at noon, and every shadow needs light.
Kpakpo clapped his hands.
“Now we can teach Mama!”
pages.alt: Kpakpo clapping joyfully beside smiling Dufie on their warmly lit veranda in the evening.
